scope: General desktop application data storage: immutable shipped-type diagnostic and opt-in compact domain records in the same actual Kael RemoteSheet/VirtualSheetGrid. Requested Rust payload only, not native RSS or cross-framework application performance.
production_change: No SharedString/ArcCow representation or Default change; no canonical benchmark model change. Public example validation, if later added, is a separate scope.

model_storage_diagnostic.scope: Actual shipped Kael SharedString versus pinned GPUI SharedString/SmolStr storage. All fixture strings fit23UTF8bytes. Three CPU process pairs plus two allocator captures; the bulk clone diagnostic is not a canonical active operation. No application CPU/RSS gap attribution.

modes: opt-in SmolStr0.3.6 business records, long heap Arc sharing through adapter

fixed_controls.semantics: All headers+logical dimensions+active coordinate+bounded cached semantics retained

same_grid_compact_domain_model.release_qualification: Strong datasets/records/query/control ownership is released after cancellation and executor drain. Reporting source wrapper, Weak control blocks, report/runtime bookkeeping and global text caches remain; no claim of zero retained process memory.
limitations: This is a headless TestPlatform settled-control retained-payload probe, not native process RSS, automatic repaint, GPU/presentation, physical input or a framework ranking.

Both canonical datasets have only<=23B values, so SmolStr0.3.6 retains them inline. Independent actual long multilingual/NUL/CRLF byte/pointer controls prove the adapter retains long heap Arc ownership but do not measure a long-valued business dataset.
Requested allocation events overlap successful realloc calls; allocator rounding/free-page retention/native resources and internal realloc old+new transient peaks are unmeasured.

Final report construction is outside stage counters. Other test/app/report owners created after the runtime baseline remain included in retained deltas. The reported bookkeeping_utf8_bytes field is a subset, not an exact total-overhead subtraction; no such subtraction is applied here.

The source-controller/counter Arc intentionally remains owned for reporting; dataset release does not claim this wrapper is dropped. Weak<Dataset> controls themselves retain small Arc control blocks. Weak-upgrade failures prove strong Dataset/records/query ownership released, not literal release of every Arc metadata allocation. Global text/runtime caches can survive window closure.
Dataset construction includes stored byte counts and four fingerprint strings; full cell/API checks outside stages still affect global transient allocation tracking but leave no retained scratch.

The controlled held-request queue temporarily owns old query data until explicitly drained; real source cancellation remains cooperative. Controller pending limits do not instantly kill non-cooperative work.
One sparse application write is keyed by original record ID+dataset identity. General asynchronous persistence/backpressure/concurrent update policies are not implemented by this probe.
Manual public viewport requests prime and evict cache tiles while the real mounted viewport remains bounded. This is not a sustained native wheel-scroll workload.

Three invalid fixture attempts are retained: default TestWindow resize lacked viewport callback; an unaligned controlled64-row request crossed2tiles; and the cancellation-channel assertion preceded executor drain. Strict assertions were preserved; no failed process contributes results. One artifact-only ambiguous-import compile error is also retained.
All production SharedString/ArcCow contracts, canonical benchmark source/model types, primary manifests and locks are unchanged by this artifact.

empty_default_rejected_lead.finding: Actual Rust1.97.1 empty Arc<str> already shares an empty allocation; no per-value heap payload or allocation. Static conversion changes observable Arc-sharing semantics, so Default remains unchanged.

compatibility: Current SharedString publicly exposes Deref and DerefMut Target=ArcCow<static,str>, and the blanket From<T:Into<ArcCow>> accepts that owned/borrowed representation. A direct SmolStr replacement would change source contracts.

Current new(impl Into<Arc<str>>) and From/Into Arc preserve shared long inputs; new_static preserves static storage. A future option must not silently copy long Arc inputs or modify generic ArcCow for unrelated users.

Prefer investigating a separately named opt-in compact application-data text type, converting only requested/visible cells to the existing UI string; evaluate real shipped workflow and migration before changing benchmark model types.

Any global SharedString representation migration requires an explicit API compatibility/version/migration decision, plus Borrow<str>/HashMap, ordering, serde, static/Arc ownership and Unicode-boundary contract tests beyond this bounded probe.
remaining_requirements: Native application performance/RSS, sustained physical scroll and full R4 comparison are separate requirements.
The sparse stable-ID write probe does not implement general asynchronous persistence, failure recovery or concurrent update/backpressure policies.
Uniform R8 total-memory policy and native assistive-technology acceptance remain open.
